# `session_unreachable_branch`: a `match` on an offered label has an arm for a label the protocol does not offer

This is a warning. A `match` on the label from `Chan.offer` has an arm
for a label that is not one of the protocol's branches. That arm can never be
taken. It is often a typo for a real label.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server

  protocol Lookup do
    choose by Server:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : String
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, sc) = Chan.new(Lookup)
    let sc2 = Chan.choose(sc, :ok)
    Chan.close(Chan.send(sc2, 7))
    let (lbl, cc2) = Chan.offer(cc)
    match lbl do
      :ok ->
        let (_n, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
      :err ->
        let (_msg, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
      :timeout ->
        ()
    end
  end
end
```

`Lookup` offers `:ok` and `:err`. The `:timeout` arm can never run.

## The fix

Remove the arm, or fix its label to the branch it was meant for:

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server

  protocol Lookup do
    choose by Server:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : String
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, sc) = Chan.new(Lookup)
    let sc2 = Chan.choose(sc, :ok)
    Chan.close(Chan.send(sc2, 7))
    let (lbl, cc2) = Chan.offer(cc)
    match lbl do
      :ok ->
        let (_n, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
      :err ->
        let (_msg, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
    end
  end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

An arm that can never be taken is dead code. When it comes from a typo,
the branch it was meant for may be left unhandled or handled by the wrong
arm. The warning shows the protocol's real labels.

See also: [choice: `choose` and `offer`](../session-types.md#choice-choose-and-offer).
